correctness.rationale: Symmetry averaging applies to unrestricted symmetric stochastic kernels; internal representations can be set to eigenvalue zero for every feasible pair of interclass edge probabilities. The quotient eigenvalue sum/product are derived directly. The universal column-omission bound proves the first phase. Beyond that, exact fixed-w norm minimization, row-capacity saturation, a concave boundary eigenvalue, and a sharp Rayleigh test-vector certificate prove both remaining phases. Regime feasibility and quotient spectra are explicitly computed. Exact-rational checker replay covers 1,462 instances but is not invoked as an infinite proof.

value.rationale: The graph is a canonical perturbation of the perfectly mixing complete graph, with a concentrated set of missing edges. The theorem computes the exact best spectral mixing performance and explicit feasible optimal kernels for every size of that deletion, exhibits a sharp capacity threshold b=a², and gives a second spectral-balance transition H=0. It is a full natural infinite classification not an arbitrary finite enumeration; it distinguishes structural damage concentration from previously solved disjoint-edge deletions.
